tiles.title: Meaningful contract examples and operation metadata

blocks.text: Use model_config = ConfigDict(json_schema_extra={"examples": [...]}) for model schema examples, or Field(examples=[...]) for field examples. Validate each proposed sample with Model.model_validate(example) before publishing it.
Body(openapi_examples={...}) supplies named request-body examples. Decorator tags, summary and description group and describe the operation; they do not change runtime behavior.

steps.title: Documentation is not a constraint override

blocks.text: A documentation sample must satisfy the executable model. Validate the synthetic order sample before putting it in schema examples or named body examples. Review the quantity bound, not just whether the payload looks plausible.
A summary can explain the operation, but cannot loosen its constraint. Ask whether the documentation illustrates the declared contract or implies a different one.

An isolated endpoint test substitutes at the declared dependency boundary. app.dependency_overrides maps the original provider callable to a replacement callable. FastAPI uses that replacement when resolving the dependency; the mapping is not keyed by a provider name or returned value.

Assign app.dependency_overrides[original] = replacement, send the HTTP request, then assert the replacement is observable in the response. In this synthetic fixture, original returns 'actual user' and replacement returns 'mock user'; the handler exposes the selected value under user.

Save and restore the previous override state in try/finally. Reset to an empty dictionary only when there were no previous overrides. An active replacement can leak into later tests; restoration is not automatic. Trace setup, request, assertion and cleanup together.
Map original callable to replacement callable, send the test request and assert the replacement is observable.
Restore the earlier override state afterward. An empty dictionary is appropriate only when the earlier state was empty.

Bind a header explicitly with Annotated[Type, Header()]. A metadata-looking parameter name alone does not select headers instead of query parameters.

Header converts underscores to hyphens by default: user_agent reads user-agent. Header names are case-insensitive. Header(alias="user-agent") explicitly chooses that name; Header(convert_underscores=False) keeps the literal user_agent mapping instead.

Annotated[Type, Cookie()] binds a cookie by name. The fixture declares cookie with a None default so omission is accepted. Source selection and omission behavior are separate: Cookie chooses the source, while the default permits absence.

steps.title: Bind a header and an omittable cookie

blocks.text: Invalid request data raises RequestValidationError. FastAPI handles it before normal operation logic receives that input. In the order fixture, the quantity value 'not an integer' cannot satisfy the declared integer field.

Assert the default status 422, then inspect response.json()["detail"]. Each relevant entry identifies the failed input location through loc and the error kind through type. The fixture derives these expectations from the unchanged contract; do not guess them.

A model-validation failure while application code builds a result, or during response validation, indicates a server-side bug. It is not the same as invalid client request data, and not every validation failure is a client 422.

blocks.code:
from fixture import client, invalid_order, validation_expectations

def evidence():
    expected_location, expected_type = validation_expectations()
    response = client.post("/orders", json=invalid_order)
    assert response.status_code == 422
    entry = response.json()["detail"][0]
    assert entry["loc"] == expected_location
    assert entry["type"] == expected_type
    return {"request": invalid_order, "status": response.status_code, "detail": response.json()["detail"]}

tiles.title: Configure established request-metrics instrumentation and verify counts, errors and latency with successful, failing and delayed requests

steps.title: Instrument the boundary and verify it

blocks.text: Use maintained instrumentation around the application boundary for request counters, response counters and a duration histogram. Handlers need not each implement their own metrics; an exposed metrics endpoint alone does not verify the wiring.

Import PrometheusMiddleware and metrics from starlette_prometheus. Register app.add_middleware(PrometheusMiddleware, filter_unhandled_paths=True), then app.add_route("/metrics/", metrics). Use bounded nonsensitive labels such as method, matched route template and response status. Filtering unmatched paths avoids unlimited series from arbitrary requested paths.

Send controlled successful, expected-error and delayed requests. Compare request and response counter changes and completed-response duration observations with those requests. This middleware updates its response counter even for a raised exception, but observes processing time only when the inner application returns a response.

left.code:
from fixture import app, CASES
from starlette_prometheus import PrometheusMiddleware, metrics

app.add_middleware(PrometheusMiddleware, filter_unhandled_paths=True)
app.add_route("/metrics/", metrics)

right.code:
from fixture import app, CASES
from httpx import AsyncClient, ASGITransport
from prometheus_client.parser import text_string_to_metric_families
from starlette_prometheus.middleware import (
    REQUESTS, RESPONSES, REQUESTS_PROCESSING_TIME,
)

METRICS = (REQUESTS._name + "_total", RESPONSES._name + "_total",
           REQUESTS_PROCESSING_TIME._name + "_count",
           REQUESTS_PROCESSING_TIME._name + "_sum")

async def snapshot(client, route):
    text = (await client.get("/metrics/")).text
    values = {}
    for family in text_string_to_metric_families(text):
        for sample in family.samples:
            if (sample.labels.get("path_template") == route
                    and sample.labels.get("method") == "GET"
                    and sample.name in METRICS):
                key = (sample.name, tuple(sorted(sample.labels.items())))
                values[key] = sample.value
    return values

async def evidence():
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app, raise_app_exceptions=False)
    rows = []
    async with app.router.lifespan_context(app):
        async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://testserver") as client:
            for case in CASES:
                route = case["route_template"]
                before = await snapshot(client, route)
                response = await client.request(case["method"], route)
                after = await snapshot(client, route)
                keys = sorted(set(before) | set(after))
                rows.append({"case": case, "actual_status": response.status_code,
                    "samples": [{"metric": key[0], "labels": dict(key[1]),
                        "before": before.get(key, 0), "after": after.get(key, 0),
                        "change": after.get(key, 0) - before.get(key, 0)} for key in keys]})
    return rows

steps.title: A response count is not a duration observation

tiles.title: Preserve input intent as contracts evolve

blocks.text: A partial update separates presence from value. Pydantic records explicitly supplied fields in model_fields_set; model_dump(exclude_unset=True) excludes fields that were not supplied.

Extract update = model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) so omitted fields do not introduce defaults that overwrite stored values. Inspect the extracted data before changing storage. A quantity-only input leaves note out of the update rather than treating its default as a supplied value.

An explicitly supplied note=None remains supplied with exclude_unset=True. A supplied string keeps its value. Adding exclude_none=True separately removes None-valued fields and can erase an intentional null update. A final model value alone cannot distinguish omission from explicit supply.

left.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel

class OrderUpdate(BaseModel):
    note: str | None = None
    quantity: int | None = None

quantity_only = OrderUpdate(quantity=2)
explicit_null = OrderUpdate(note=None)
concrete_note = OrderUpdate(note='Leave at reception')

right.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel

class OrderUpdate(BaseModel):
    note: str | None = None
    quantity: int | None = None

quantity_only = OrderUpdate(quantity=2)
explicit_null = OrderUpdate(note=None)
concrete_note = OrderUpdate(note='Leave at reception')

def evidence():
    for name, model in [("note omitted", quantity_only),
                        ("explicit null note", explicit_null),
                        ("concrete note", concrete_note)]:
        yield {"case": name, "model_fields_set": sorted(model.model_fields_set),
               "exclude_unset": model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True),
               "exclude_unset_and_none": model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True, exclude_none=True)}

import json
for row in evidence():
    print(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False))

blocks.takeaway: Inspect supplied fields and execute the extraction; exclude_none removes null separately from omission.

steps.title: Omission and null are different updates

blocks.text: Compare the registered cases: quantity-only input, explicit note=None, and note='Leave at reception'. model_fields_set reveals what was supplied; model_dump(exclude_unset=True) extracts those fields without omitted defaults. This preserves the difference between leaving note unchanged and supplying a replacement value.

exclude_unset asks whether a field was supplied. exclude_none asks whether its value is None. They are not interchangeable cleanup flags: adding exclude_none can remove the explicit null that the update contract intended to preserve.

steps.title: Extract updates without losing null intent

blocks.text: Compatibility review compares old client expectations, not just matching type names. Changing an omittable note field into a required field rejects previously accepted requests that omit it. Compare requiredness as well as types.

Tightening a type or field constraint can reject previously valid input. Test representative old inputs against the revised model. The registered comparison keeps an old quantity sample alongside the previous and tightened constraints, so both validations can be inspected.

Removing or changing a public response field or operation can change documented client expectations. Compare the generated paths and response schemas against the previous contract before approving the revision. Matching input type names alone says nothing about those public output changes.

blocks.takeaway: Compare old inputs and generated public schemas, not just type names.
